paper.title_en: Feasibility Studies Using Enhanced Particle Production: An Afterburner for the MPD Experiment
paper.abstract_en: Anisotropic flow and global polarization are the key observables for characterizing properties of strongly-interacting matter in relativistic heavy-ion collisions at NICA energies ($\sqrt {{{s}_{{NN}}}} $ = 2.5-11 GeV). A significant challenge for the MPD experiment is achieving the necessary statistical precision for these measurements, particularly for direct photons, ϕ-mesons, $\Sigma $ and Λ hyperons. To address this issue, we have developed a statistical event resampling afterburner package. This tool was validated using simulated Xe + Xe collisions at $\sqrt {{{s}_{{NN}}}} $ = 2.87 GeV generated with the UrQMD model. The application of this afterburner package resulted in a substantial enhancement of the resolution of the directed (${{v}_{1}}$) and elliptic (${{v}_{2}}$) flow of Λ hyperons, in addition to their global polarization. This work confirms the method's utility for the future feasibility studies and data analysis in the MPD experiment.
